result.rationale: The migration inserts old setting values verbatim via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without running EmbeddableHost's before_validation, which strips schemes/paths only on save. Since `record_for_host` matches via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, a migrated row like 'http://discourse.org' can never equal a URI host like 'discourse.org', and CRLF '\r' from split("\n") would also break exact matching — silently breaking embedding for existing sites.

adjudication.rationale: The migration inserts each line from the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` directly into `embeddable_hosts.host` via raw SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without any normalization (no model callbacks run). If existing values include schemes like `http://discourse.org` or include `\r` from CRLF (since it splits only on `"\n"`), those rows will be stored verbatim. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the request URL and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, i.e. it compares against just `discourse.org`, which will not match a stored `http://discourse.org` (or `discourse.org\r`). This would cause previously-working hosts to fail authorization after upgrade, while the admin UI would still show the raw stored host as if valid.
